content: The dosage of Penicillin V potassium should be carefully determined based on the sensitivity of the infecting microorganisms and the severity of the infection. It should also be adjusted according to the patient’s clinical response. Below are the specific dosage recommendations for adults and children aged 12 years and older: 1. Streptococcal Infections: For mild to moderately severe infections of the upper respiratory tract, including conditions such as scarlet fever and erysipelas, the recommended dose is 125 to 250 mg (equivalent to 200,000 to 400,000 units) every 6 to 8 hours for a duration of 10 days. 2. Pneumococcal Infections: For mild to moderately severe infections of the respiratory tract, including otitis media, the recommended dose is 250 to 500 mg (equivalent to 400,000 to 800,000 units) every 6 hours. Treatment should continue until the patient has been free of fever for at least 2 days. 3. Staphylococcal Infections: For mild infections of the skin and soft tissues, the recommended dose is 250 to 500 mg (equivalent to 400,000 to 800,000 units) every 6 to 8 hours. It is essential to perform culture and sensitivity testing to confirm the susceptibility of the organism. 4. Fusospirochetosis (Vincent’s Infection) of the Oropharynx: For mild to moderately severe infections, the recommended dose is 250 to 500 mg (equivalent to 400,000 to 800,000 units) every 6 to 8 hours. 5. Prevention of Recurrence Following Rheumatic Fever and/or Chorea: To prevent recurrence, the recommended dose is 125 to 250 mg (equivalent to 200,000 to 400,000 units) administered twice daily on a continuous basis. 6. Prophylaxis Against Bacterial Endocarditis: For patients with congenital heart disease, rheumatic heart disease, or other acquired valvular heart conditions undergoing dental or upper respiratory tract surgical procedures, the recommended prophylactic dose is: Adults: 2 grams of Penicillin V taken 1 hour before the procedure, followed by 1 gram 6 hours later. Children under 60 lbs: 1 gram of Penicillin V taken 1 hour before the procedure, followed by 500 mg 6 hours later.
